name: Business Manager (BM) in a PM²-Agile Project
one_liner: Project Owner's delegate who empowers and aligns the Product Owner.
purpose: As defined in PM², the Business Manager coordinates client-side activities and roles and ensures the project's deliverables fulfil business and user needs. Adopting PM²-Agile clearly extends the BM's range of action, because the new Product Owner role creates a permanent and active client's voice on the provider's side. The BM must empower the PrOw for day-to-day decisions and keep the PrOw aligned with the BM and the Business Implementation Group.
meta: Managing layer — delegate of the Project Owner, unchanged by PM²-Agile
The PrOw's permanent client voice inside the Agile Project Core Team
Empower the PrOw and keep the Work Items List aligned to business strategy

rasci.title: BM in the guide's RAM (RASCI) tables
rows: Release Plan / Iteration Plan / Development Work Plan
legend: Responsible — does the work and leads those who support
Accountable — authorises and approves; only one person
Supports — works with the Responsible person to complete it
Consulted — provides input to the activity

items: Coordination of client-side activities and roles — user and business representatives
Assurance that deliverables fulfil the business and user needs
The Business Case (Responsible, in the PM² RAM)
The empowerment of the Product Owner for day-to-day decisions
Alignment of the Work Items List with business strategy, with the BIG
How far the Product Owner is empowered to decide without waiting
Business priorities and objectives fed into the Work Items List
With the Project Manager, when to intervene on misaligned expectations
Manage the Work Items List — supports, explaining context changes affecting the list
Work Items List prioritisation — supports, determining priorities with the PrOw
Iteration Review — consulted on demonstrated and new or deleted work items
Informed of WIL refinement outputs, the updated Release Plan and iteration goals
Own or prioritise the Work Items List — the PrOw is Responsible and Accountable
Act as the single voice of the stakeholders — that is the PrOw's role
Attend the Daily Stand-up — the RAM marks the BM N/A there
Accept or reject iteration output — the PrOw accepts against acceptance criteria
Manage the A-PCT or its plans — that stays with the team, TeCo and PM

fields.what: Plays a vital role coordinating client-side activities and roles such as user and business representatives.
fields.pollux: Hopper keeps Lending Operations' representatives lined up behind the portal.

fields.what: Ensures the project's deliverables fulfil the business and user needs, as defined in PM².
fields.pollux: Holds the portal to the five success criteria in the Business Case.

fields.what: PM²-Agile clearly extends the BM's range of action because the PrOw creates a permanent client voice on the provider's side.
fields.pollux: Hopper gains a daily voice inside the team she did not have on CASTOR.

fields.what: The PrOw becomes the right person to act as liaison between the User Representatives and the provider organisation.
fields.pollux: Curie carries reporting-analyst feedback into the team every fortnight.

fields.what: The prioritised Work Items List reflects the client organisation's strategy and needs, produced by URs and PrOw in refinement.
fields.pollux: The list encodes what Risk, Finance and the Board each need from reporting.

fields.what: The PrOw ensures User Representatives participate actively in the Iteration Review to validate the iteration output.
fields.pollux: Analysts validate the reconciliation panel before Release 2 on 28 Jun 2029.

fields.what: Must empower the PrOw to take the day-to-day decisions that let the team progress without waiting for specific decisions.
fields.pollux: Hopper empowers Curie; the team never waits a fortnight for an answer.

fields.what: Must keep the PrOw aligned with the BM and the BIG so the Work Items List reflects the business strategy and vision.
fields.pollux: Alignment sessions keep Curie's priorities inside the agreed release strategy.

fields.what: Supports the Product Owner in determining the priorities of the Work Items List; the PrOw stays Responsible and Accountable.
fields.pollux: Conflict 3 — on Release 2, Curie decides and Hopper supports.

fields.what: Supports the Manage Work Items List activity by explaining how changes to the solution or organisation context affect the list.
fields.pollux: Flags that a new national-authority requirement changes Release 3 content.

fields.what: Consulted about the demonstrated items and about new or deleted work items arising from the review.
fields.pollux: Comments on the demonstrated exposure views without accepting them.

fields.what: Informed by the PrOw of refinement outputs and the updated Release Plan, and of iteration goals by PrOw and PM.
fields.pollux: Hopper learns each iteration goal without sitting in the planning.

fields.what: Together with the Project Manager, may intervene when expectations are not aligned or the PrOw and team cannot reach consensus.
fields.pollux: You and Hopper intervene only when Curie and the team deadlock.

fields.what: In the PM² organisation the BM is the Project Owner's delegate in the managing layer and collaborates with the PM.
fields.pollux: Hopper represents Nightingale, who stays accountable for the benefits.

fields.what: In the PM² RAM the BM is Responsible for the Business Case, with the Project Owner accountable.
fields.pollux: The Business Case approved 12 Oct 2028 argues why agile, not just faster.

traps: The BM does not become the Product Owner; PM²-Agile extends the BM's range of action.
An unempowered Product Owner is the failure mode — the team waits for BM decisions.
BM supports WIL prioritisation; the PrOw is Responsible and Accountable for it.
The BM is N/A in the Daily Stand-up RAM, not merely informed.
The BM represents the Project Owner; the PrOw represents stakeholders inside the team.
